item.title: ‘It’s frustrating’: Kamala Harris slams prosecution of James Comey
item.description: Kamala Harris sharply criticized the federal indictment of former FBI director James Comey, viewing it as President Trump's drive to punish political enemies. Comey faces charges of obstruction and perjury linked to his Russia inquiry testimony, following Trump's public demands for his prosecution. This action has raised alarms among Democrats and legal experts about the weaponization of the Justice Department.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Kimmel’s late-night show back: Nexstar, Sinclair end weeklong blackout
item.description: Jimmy Kimmel's show returned after Nexstar and Sinclair ended a week-long blackout, initially imposed over Kimmel's comments on Charlie Kirk's killing. Disney-owned ABC had also suspended Kimmel following an FCC warning. The resolution came after discussions, highlighting free speech debates and the financial pressures on local affiliates.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘A monster’: Arizona man convicted of killing eight in deadly 2017 spree; motive still unclear
item.description: An Arizona jury convicted Cleophus Cooksey Jr. of murdering eight people in a 2017 three-week shooting spree, marking him as one of the state’s most prolific serial killers. His victims included random individuals, his mother, and stepfather. Cooksey, 43, now faces the death penalty following convictions for murder, kidnapping, sexual assault, and armed robbery.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'America first': US Supreme Court sides with Trump; $4B foreign aid withheld
item.description: The US Supreme Court sided with President Trump, allowing his administration to withhold roughly $4 billion in foreign aid approved by Congress, aligning with his "America First" agenda. This ruling temporarily blocks a lower court injunction. Liberal justices dissented, arguing the decision undermines the constitutional separation of powers, though the court noted it's not a final determination on the merits.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

Bibi delivers defiant speech at UN after walkout by dozens of nations
item.description: Israeli PM Netanyahu, in a defiant UN address, defended his nation's actions and pledged to "finish the job" against Hamas. He sharply criticised US allies for recognising a Palestinian state, labelling it a reward for terrorism and asserting Israel's refusal to accept a "terrorist state." Amid delegate walkouts, Netanyahu accused leaders of succumbing to pressure, while privately acknowledging Israel's intelligence.

item.title: Want to bring a dog to this Italian city? That'll be $1.75
Live ammunition used against Nepal protesters, forensics show
item.description: Medical examinations confirm at least 33 Nepalese anti-corruption protesters died from "live bullets" fired by "high-velocity firearms," marking the first official acknowledgment of such force. This revelation follows unrest that killed 74 and injured thousands, ultimately leading to PM KP Sharma Oli's resignation. The findings contradict Oli's earlier claims, intensifying scrutiny on the government's response to the demonstrations.

item.title: ‘Study my brain’: NFL shooter who killed four confirmed to have CTE; accused league of hiding brain injury risks
item.description: Shane Tamura, who killed four people at NFL headquarters, including an NYPD officer, was confirmed to have CTE. He had requested his brain be studied, accusing the NFL of concealing brain injury dangers. Tamura then took his own life after the rampage.

item.title: ‘Don’t use unless absolutely necessary’: Donald Trump reiterates Tylenol claim; proposes suggestions on other vaccines
item.description: Former US President Donald Trump reiterated controversial health warnings, advising pregnant women against Tylenol and urging major changes to childhood vaccination schedules. He recommended separating MMR shots, delaying Hepatitis B vaccines until age 12, and administering vaccines over multiple visits.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘About justice, not revenge’: Donald Trump slams James Comey following indictment, backs justice department; claims he ‘lied a lot’
item.description: Donald Trump defended the Justice Department and criticized James Comey following his indictment for false statements and obstruction. Trump asserted it was about justice, not revenge, labeling Comey a "dirty cop" and suggesting more officials could face charges. He accused Democrats of weaponizing the DOJ, while his own past indictments were dropped.

item.title: Dubai Police warn of new scam: Fake consumer protection sites stealing personal data and banking info
item.description: Dubai Police have alerted the public about a new online scam where fraudsters create fake “Consumer Protection” websites on search engines and social media. These sites deceive users into downloading malicious apps, allowing scammers to remotely access personal data and conduct unauthorized financial transactions. The Anti-Fraud Department warns users to stay cautious and protect their mobile information.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘Nothing to lose but our chains’: Assata Shakur, former Black Liberation Army member, dies in Cuba; remained on ‘most wanted list’
item.description: Assata Shakur, the former Black Panther and Black Liberation Army member convicted of a 1973 New Jersey state trooper's murder, has died in Havana at 78. She maintained her innocence, escaped prison, and received political asylum in Cuba, despite being on the "Most Wanted List." Cuban officials confirmed her death was due to health complications and advanced age.

item.title: Who is Lindsey Halligan? Donald Trump’s former lawyer and Erika Kirk ally, now prosecuting James Comey
item.description: Newly appointed US attorney Lindsey Halligan announced the indictment of former FBI director James Comey on obstruction and perjury charges, citing a "breach of public trust." Halligan, who previously defended Donald Trump and joined his legal team after meeting him in 2021, emphasized that "no one is above the law.
